newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Retail buyers ramp up Singapore stocks at close.
newsitem.headline: Retail buyers ramp up Singapore stocks at close.

text.p: Continued retail fever pushed the Singapore stock market back into positive territory at the close on Wednesday, dealers said.
Activity was centred on speculative Malaysian shares traded over the counter (OTC) like Berjaya Group, they said.
The diversified Malaysian property company saw prices ending at a new year high of Singapore $1.98, up S$0.17 on more than 10 million shares.
Keen retail interest also ramped up activity in fruit and vegetable supplier, FHTK Holdings. The share ended up S$0.075 at S$0.775 in hectic trade of over 49 million shares.
The key Straits Times Industrials Index ended up at the day's high of 2,246.99, up 17.20 points. Turnover was an active 434.7 million shares, with gainers leading losers by 325 to 101.
Creative Technology rose S$1.20 to S$19.10.

Institutions took profit late in the day, sending property heavyweights like City Development and DBS Land lower. CityDev led losers, ending S$0.30 down at S$14.30. The property index fell 8.05 points to end at 788.54.
"Property, retail stocks came off as they were not expected to post good earnings next month," said a dealer, noting that these shares had firmed recently. -- Angela Tan (65 8703083)
